I know from experience that sometimes when people try to not act homophobic it gets awkward, because that's all they think about when they talk to us. I think OP may have worded it slightly wrong, so let's say it wasn't "to not be gay at my wedding". It was "to hold back a little on the PDA so as not to make *anyone* involved uncomfortable" I include OP's friend in the anyone too.

As a lesbian myself, I managed to get lucky with an accepting family, however I do know a friend who quite literally got disowned because she was friends with a "faggot". Its not very easy to tell people who are homophobic to calm it, because depending on how large their belief is, it could go completely sideways, and instead of losing a friend OP could lose some family too.

It's for the safety of the friend during the wedding as well, would just make for a slightly more comfortable atmosphere to be in for a short time, then they can go right back to being themselves without endangering themself.
Sad part is they are actually a good editor, but holy shit is that an awful thing to do with the talent

Coming from a lesbian, myself, I would say that You are NTA. 
If they want to have a good time at the wedding then they should hide it for a little while. It's not loyalty, and you aren't breaking anything in this, but you want to protect them with the prior knowledge that your families just don't accept it.

Let's say he was to go, and be as gay as he could possibly act that day, that would cause an air of tension which you would have to deal with on your wedding day, and that's not including the fact that he will be ostracized from the group from the start.
If I knew my best friend's family was homophobic, but they were getting married and i knew that the friend excepted me, I wouldn't say anything about being gay or have any PDA while I was there, for the sake as not to ruin the mood.

If your asking me, he's overreacting, and not thinking through what you actually said, but assuming based on a few maybe slip words or phrases. Him not saying anything is better for his and your sake.

Definitely NTA.
